item.title: Qatar Is Not Mediating U.S.-Iran Talks, Foreign Minister Says
item.summary: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry warned that the regional security system has been shattered, as the war has destroyed trust between Gulf countries and Iran.

item.title: Why President Trump Has a Big Oil Problem
item.summary: Our national security correspondent David E. Sanger looks at President Trump’s trouble handling retaliatory attacks by Iran that have largely choked off the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Iran’s New Security Chief Is a Hard-Line Former Guards Commander
item.summary: Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr replaces Ali Larijani, who was killed last week in an Israeli strike. He has a history of expanding the Guards’ reach into Iran’s politics.

item.title: Trump’s Threat to ‘Obliterate’ Iran’s Power Stations Could Constitute a War Crime, Rights Experts Say
item.summary: Intentionally targeting the country’s energy infrastructure could constitute a war crime under international law.

item.title: Three of the Lives Lost in One Day of Israeli Strikes in Lebanon
item.summary: A 4-year-old, a professor and an aid worker are among those killed in separate airstrikes as Israel pummels towns and cities, saying it is targeting Hezbollah operatives.

item.title: War in Iran Is Disrupting Air Travel, Hitting Middle East Hardest
item.summary: Some airlines and travelers, especially in the Middle East and elsewhere in Asia, are bearing the brunt of the pain, while others are doing better.

item.title: Saudi Leader Is Said to Push Trump to Continue Iran War in Recent Calls
item.summary: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman sees a “historic opportunity” to remake the region, according to people briefed by U.S. officials on the conversations.

item.title: Pentagon Officials Weigh Deployment of Airborne Troops for Iran War
item.summary: The combat forces would come from a brigade of about 3,000 soldiers capable of deploying anywhere in the world within 18 hours.

item.title: Trump Delays Energy Strikes, but Iran’s Infrastructure Is Already Battered
item.summary: U.S. and Israeli attacks on power plants and other civilian infrastructure risk escalating the conflict across the region, and angering Iranians who oppose the government.

item.title: Energy Crisis Will Not Be Resolved Quickly if War Ends, I.E.A. Chief Warns
item.summary: Fatih Birol, the leader of the International Energy Agency, said the Iran war was a bigger crisis than the two oil shocks in the 1970s combined.
